1.explanation:
1. We import Accordion/AccordionItem from carbon-components-react and Footer/FooterNavGroup from @carbon/react in the same React tree.
2. Both components call the internal useId hook without sharing a common prefix, so they each generate id="accordion-item-1" on their panels.
3. Shrink your browser width (below the Footer’s collapse-breakpoint) so the FooterNavGroup renders as an expandable section using the same id logic.
4. Open DevTools and search for “#accordion-item-1” – you will see the id duplicated on both the accordion panel and the footer nav panel, triggering an accessibility warning.
1.bug_scenario: On a single page we render an Accordion (from carbon-components-react) and a Footer with collapsible groups (from @carbon/react). Both components internally use the same useId hook to generate ids like “accordion-item-1”, so you end up with two elements in the DOM sharing the same id. When you open DevTools and search for “#accordion-item-1” you see the AccordionItem panel and the FooterNavGroup panel both have id="accordion-item-1", causing an accessibility violation.
